title: Density-dependent and environmental drivers of the growth of one year old Gulf of Riga (Baltic Sea) spring spawning herring
content:
Abstract
We analyzed a multi-decadal time series (1961–2020) to identify the drivers of individual growth of age-1 of the Gulf of Riga spring spawning herring. The study covered the longest period of investigation to date for this stock, allowing investigation of variable ecosystem conditions and regimes. Density-dependent and prey factors, spawning stock biomass (SSB) and the abundance of age-1 herring, had the strongest effects on individual fish growth throughout the study period. In addition, the effects of different developmental stages of small copepods (Eurytemora affinis affinis and Acartia spp.) were also significant. In general, the highest individual growth of the fish was observed at low SSB and age-1 abundance levels in combination with moderate to high food densities. Across two distinct ecosystem regimes, different prey variables appeared as significant predictors of herring individual growth. Structural equation modelling showed that climate variables had indirect effects on fish growth mediated through prey abundance. Our results demonstrate the value of long-term data collection and monitoring for detecting such effects at multi-annual and multi-decadal scales. They can potentially contribute to a better understanding of environmental forcing on commercial fish populations and the inclusion of ecosystem information in fish stock assessment and advice.
